'''Theodore William Gamelin''' is an American mathematician. He is a [[professor emeritus]] of mathematics at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]].<ref name="ucla"/>

Gamelin was born in 1939. He received his B.S. degree in mathematics from [[Yale University]] in 1960,<ref name="ucla">{{cite web|url=https://www.math.ucla.edu/~twg/vita.html|publisher=math.ucla.edu|title=Theodore W. Gamelin|accessdate=2017-02-05}}</ref>
and completed his Ph.D. at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1963. His doctoral advisor was [[František Wolf]]. His doctoral dissertation was titled ''The extension problem for restrictions of functions in a subspace of C(X)''.<ref name="ams">{{cite web|url=http://www.genealogy.ams.org/id.php?id=32792|publisher=genealogy.ams.org|title=Theodore Gamelin - The Mathematics Genealogy Project|accessdate=2017-02-05}}</ref>
He served as [[C.L.E. Moore Instructor]] at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] from 1963 to 1965, before joining the UCLA faculty.<ref name="ucla"/>

In 2012, he became one of the inaugural [[Fellow]]s of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2017-04-12</ref>
